answer: Picture the registry as a jetty where every arriving hull must forge its own mooring ring before tying up: each epoch, each identity faces a fresh interactive reasoning puzzle drawn from a private seed, so solutions cannot be copied between accounts. A farmer running N puppets must crack N distinct marble-hard problems, paying N times the compute and latency, while an honest single agent solves just one. Launching hulls is free, but every one must sail the narrows alone, so the flood meant to swamp the dock stalls in its own queue.
